## Lecturer

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="25%"}
![Tobias Wildi](https://ui-avatars.com/api/?name=Tobias+Wildi&size=200&background=1e3a5f&color=ffffff){width=200px}

::: {.column width="75%"}

**Tobias Wildi** is a historian and archival scientist. He is senior consultant and chairman of the board of docuteam AG, the archival services company he co-founded in 2003 and managed until 2020, and he teaches digital preservation, records management and information management at several academic institutions. From 2021 to 2024 he was Full Professor for archival studies at FH Graubünden. He studied history, political science and computer science at the Universities of Zurich and Lausanne and received his doctorate from the University of Zurich in 2002. Since 2019 he has been a member of the Experts Group on Archival Description (EGAD) of the International Council on Archives, where he works on the Records in Contexts ontology (RiC-O). From 2016 to 2023 he chaired the Swiss Federal Commission for the Protection of Cultural Heritage.

*Recorded during his professorship at FH Graubünden.*

## Lecture Overview

## Overview

Wildi introduces archives as institutions of long-term evidence, memory, and accountability. He explains how archives differ from libraries, how archival collections are structured, and why digital preservation is now a central archival task.

## Main Points

- Archives preserve selected records because they retain evidential value and future research value.
- Public archives play an important democratic role by enabling long-term traceability of administrative and governmental action.
- The lecture distinguishes archival records from copyrighted works and explains why this matters conceptually and institutionally.
- Two core archival principles structure collections: provenance and original order.
- Digital preservation is defined as keeping digital information usable across changing generations of hardware, software, file formats, and systems.

## Examples Mentioned

- The Swiss Federal Archives
- City, economic, and specialized archives
- Hierarchical archival description
- Long-term preservation of records from databases and records management systems
